content.user_title: Draft ISO 27001 Documents for Belgian SMEs
content.value_statement: Belgian SMEs need consistent security documentation for audits and customer reviews. This guide helps an AI assistant draft ISMS scope, risk assessments, applicability statements, and policies.
actual_capabilities: Guides drafting of ISMS scope, organizational context, interested parties, and boundaries.
Outlines likelihood-times-impact risk assessments and treatment plans with named risk owners.
Guides Statement of Applicability drafting with justifications for Annex A control inclusion and exclusion.
Supports drafting access control, supplier security, incident response, business continuity, and secure development policies.
Introduces a preliminary Belgian NIS2 quickcheck through questions about sector, turnover, and employee count.
limitations: Only the public guidance file is included; original scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
Generated documents do not provide certification or replace internal audits, management review, and an accredited certification audit.
The NIS2 quickcheck is preliminary guidance, not a verified determination of legal applicability.
Outputs depend on supplied organizational facts; the guide does not verify implemented controls or supporting evidence.

use_cases.title: Prepare a first certification documentation set
use_cases.description: Draft scope, risk treatment, and applicability documents for a Belgian SME preparing its first ISO 27001 audit.

use_cases.title: Prepare customer security responses
use_cases.description: Develop draft security policies to support customer questionnaire responses, clearly separating implemented practices from planned controls.

use_cases.title: Review an ISMS after organizational changes
use_cases.description: Identify document updates following supplier or scope changes, including revised risk owners and control applicability justifications.

prompt_templates.title: Begin with an ISMS scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Help draft an ISMS scope for our Belgian IT company with 15 employees. Ask about services, locations, systems, interested parties, and boundaries first.

prompt_templates.title: Build a risk register
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a risk register for these assets and processes: [details]. Propose likelihood and impact scales, treatment actions, and owners. Label assumptions for review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: document risk assessment and treatment.

prompt_templates.title: Draft control applicability decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use our scope and risk register: [details]. Draft an ISO 27001:2022 Statement of Applicability. Explain proposed inclusions and exclusions. Mark missing evidence and unresolved decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect risks to Annex A control decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a supplier change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these ISMS documents against our supplier change: [details]. Identify scope, risk treatment, applicability, and policy updates. Flag NIS2 questions for qualified review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess documentation changes across the ISMS.

output_examples.input: Draft an initial scope outline for a Belgian IT SME with 15 employees and outsourced hosting.
output: Scope draft: IT service delivery and supporting information systems; specific services and locations require confirmation.
Interested parties: customers, employees, hosting providers, and relevant authorities.
Boundary question: Which hosting responsibilities belong to the provider, and which remain with the SME?
Open decisions: confirm legal entity, covered services, locations, exclusions, and scope owner.

output_examples.input: Create a draft risk entry for loss of access to our outsourced hosting provider.
output: Risk: provider disruption prevents access to hosted services.
Provisional assessment: likelihood 2 and impact 4 on proposed five-point scales; score 8 requires organizational validation.
Proposed treatment: review recovery commitments, maintain independent backups, and test restoration.
Proposed owner: IT operations lead, subject to assignment.
Evidence needed: supplier agreement, backup records, restoration test results, and documented risk acceptance.

best_practices: Provide accurate services, assets, suppliers, locations, and responsibilities before requesting drafts.
Have control owners validate risk scores, treatment actions, applicability decisions, and supporting evidence.
Verify current Belgian NIS2 requirements with authoritative sources and qualified advisers before making compliance decisions.
anti_patterns: Treating generated documents as proof of certification or implemented security controls.
Determining NIS2 applicability from employee count alone.
Publishing generic policies without confirming responsibilities, operational practices, and evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill provide ISO 27001 certification?
faq.answer: No. It supports documentation drafting. Certification requires an accredited certification audit, alongside internal audits and management review.

faq.question: Which ISO 27001 edition does the guide target?
faq.answer: The guide targets ISO 27001:2022 and describes coverage of its 93 Annex A controls.

faq.question: Are the original scripts and templates included?
faq.answer: No. This package contains only the public guidance file, not the original scripts, extension source, or templates.

faq.question: Can the NIS2 quickcheck determine our legal obligations?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as preliminary guidance and verify applicability against current Belgian requirements with qualified advice.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this guidance?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Output quality depends on the assistant and the organizational information supplied.

faq.question: What should we provide before requesting documents?
faq.answer: Provide your legal entity, services, locations, assets, suppliers, existing controls, and responsible owners. Clearly label unknown facts and planned practices.
